packages.label: אָדָם וְהַסֵּדֶר הָאֱלֹקִי
packages.reason: All these concepts share the same essential nature: they are the divine principle of completeness, order, and life-force. 'Adam' = YHVH spelled out with alphs (gematria 45 = mah) = divine sekhel/wisdom that animates all things. 'Mah' (humility/divinity), 'sekhel', 'chiyut', 'shleimut', 'miluyi' are all different names for the same reality — divine wisdom that fills and gives life. The aleph-bet in order (kedem), the letter yud (=10, the wisdom of the divine), and kaf (= yud by gematria) represent the ordered, complete, masculine divine principle. 'Davar she-nimshakh mi-makom gavoah' and 'shvi' express the same reality of drawing down this divine order into one's consciousness.

merge_notes.reason: This pair (Component F in the raw graph) is a small isolated component. The proof text explains 'ושבית שביו — כשתהיה בבחינת מה, כשתמשיך לך אלקות' — the shvi (captive/drawn-down thing) is explicitly equated with drawing down the 'mah' (Adam/divine sekhel). The concept of 'shvi' is the act of attaching divine order into one's consciousness, which is the very substance of this good package. Shvi is not a new domain — it is an aspect of how Adam/mah is drawn down.

packages.label: חַוָּה וּמַלְכוּת
packages.label_en: Chava and Malkhut — the Feminine Vessel
packages.reason: All these concepts share the same essential nature: they are the feminine receptive principle — the vessel that receives from the masculine divine source. Chava = malkhut peh = Oral Torah = dibur (speech) = eretz (earth) = dalet (the letter that has nothing of its own). Ahor = Tashrak (reverse alphabet) = 'shelo ke-seder' (the disordered state of Chava when separated from Adam). Malkhut = dalet (as the source text says: 'malkhut ha-nikra dalet, leit lah mi-garmah klum'). This is a neutral package because the same vessel/entity (Chava/malkhut) can be either ordered (when connected to Adam/God) or disordered (when separated). The Torah's entire teaching revolves around this vessel and its two orientations.

merge_notes.reason: Component C in the raw graph. The proof text explicitly equates אחור = תשרק = שלא כסדר = חוה: 'אחור הוא בחינת תשרק שלא כסדר. וזה בחינת אדם וחוה, כסדר ושלא כסדר.' Tashrak (backward alphabet) is simply the same concept as 'ahor' and both are the same as Chava/malkhut in its disordered/reversed mode.

Component E in the raw graph. The proof text explicitly states: 'מלכות הנקרא דלת, לית לה מגרמה כלום' — malkhut is called dalet because it has nothing of its own. Malkhut here is the same concept as Chava (the Torah explicitly equates them throughout: 'זאת הבחינה מלכות, חוה'), and the dalet is its letter-symbol.

packages.label: שֶׁלֹּא כְּסֵדֶר וּמִלְחָמָה
packages.reason: All these concepts share the same essential nature: they are the pathological state of separation from divine order. 'Lo ke-seder' (disorder) = 'milchama' (war) = 'hitnagdut ha-ratzon' (opposition of wills) — these are all the same experience of inner/outer conflict arising when Chava/malkhut is separated from Adam/sekhel. 'Davay' (sickness/faintness of heart) is the symptomatic suffering-state that results from this disorder. The Torah explicitly states: 'kol milchama hu hitnagdut ha-ratzon, hu bechina shelo ke-seder.'
